idiom_name: Twirl templates compiled to Scala functions plus plain helper objects under views/helper
implementation_notes: Twirl compiles every template into a Scala function (views.html.<pkg>.<name>.apply), so the boundary between view and logic is a normal function call: a helper is a plain object or function returning Html, conventionally kept in a views/helper package, and reusable blocks can also be declared inside a template - Play's own guidance is to externalise anything complex into a Scala class instead of growing template code. There is no helper registry to maintain: the compiler checks each call, formatting comes from java.text/java.time, and the helper remains a pure function of its arguments.
pitfalls: Html(...) marks the string as safe markup; wrapping user-supplied data in Html is the standard XSS route in Twirl - use @-interpolation and let the template escape values instead.
java.text.NumberFormat is mutable and not thread-safe, so a shared formatter used by concurrently rendered templates is a data race; build it per call or keep it thread-confined.
Twirl compiles templates as part of the build, so every helper signature change rebuilds all call sites - safe, but it makes helpers a compile-time dependency of the views package.
